agenda: Check Mei and the platform team workload
Examine Q4 scope against engineering capacity
Discuss two backend hires and Mei’s director path
Improve the product and engineering planning cadence

chapters.title: Platform Load and Recovery
beats: Mei says three platform engineers have handled eleven after-hours pages in two weeks, with Lucas pulled into ETA incidents and no recovery time after the optimizer outage.
Priya asks whether the load is a temporary spike or an ownership problem; Mei says the shared rotation hides chronic support work.
They agree Mei will document the rotation and protect an afternoon of recovery time this week.

chapters.title: Q4 Scope and Capacity
beats: Priya outlines tomorrow’s proposed bets: driver mobile v2, an ETA model, and a staged self-serve onboarding pilot.
Mei argues that promising all three at full scope while platform reliability work remains open will recreate the same burnout.
They agree to take a capacity-based proposal to Q4 planning, with the onboarding pilot gated behind support and error-rate evidence.

chapters.title: Backend Hiring and Leadership
beats: Mei wants two backend engineers, one senior engineer for platform ownership and one engineer for onboarding integrations, but neither can be counted as immediate capacity.
Priya asks Mei to show recruiting milestones and a thirty-day onboarding plan instead of treating headcount as a Q4 delivery guarantee.
Mei describes her goal of growing toward a director role and asks for ownership of cross-team capacity planning and candid feedback.

chapters.title: Planning Together and Next Steps
beats: Mei says engineering often receives a finished roadmap after customer priorities are already presented as promises.
Priya accepts the feedback and proposes a joint product-engineering scoping session before future planning commitments.
They close with named follow-ups for a capacity note, hiring brief, shared planning experiment, and Mei’s growth plan.
